title: Repository Instructions
heading: Repository Instructions
text:
Repository Instructions
These instructions apply to every human contributor and AI coding agent, whatever tool is used. `AGENTS.md` files are the only repository instruction source; tool-specific files may only help a tool discover them ([agent instructions](docs/architecture/agent-instructions.md)).

title: Repository Instructions
heading: Global invariants
text:
Global invariants
The repository is the primary source of truth. Keep implementation, schemas, contracts, tests, documentation, and generated artifacts consistent. Do not invent undocumented behavior or treat planned directories and capabilities as implemented.
Use English for source, identifiers, comments, documentation, commit-facing artifacts, database/API descriptions, logs, error codes, tests, scripts, and tooling, except where product localization or external data explicitly requires another language.
Inspect relevant files and existing patterns before editing. Make the smallest coherent change, preserve unrelated work, and explain assumptions that cannot be verified. Prefer the least irreversible solution when uncertain.
Respect architectural boundaries and accepted ADRs. Search for an existing equivalent before introducing abstractions, dependencies, or cross-layer relationships. Shared code must represent shared meaning. Report architectural conflicts rather than silently bypassing them; significant new decisions require an ADR.
Keep one canonical source where practical. Change sources and regenerate derived artifacts instead of hand-editing generated references. Reviewed SQL migrations follow their separate authorship and release rules.
Update tests and affected documentation when behavior changes. Never weaken validation, typing, tests, security, or observability merely to make a change pass. Verify at the appropriate boundary and report remaining errors or unavailable checks honestly.
Treat external input as untrusted. Preserve secure defaults and server-side enforcement. Never commit or log secrets, expose internal stack traces to end users, or disable controls for convenience. Expected failures must be explicit and unexpected failures observable.
For implementation work, follow and maintain this repository's implementation plan and human-action checklist, linked from the README's [Current state](README.md#current-state). Update affected task/phase statuses, evidence, and dependencies as work progresses and before handoff; record and surface human blockers instead of silently skipping them. Neither document authorizes work beyond the current task.

Commands and current state
The pnpm workspace, local validation tooling, CI configuration, the API runtime with composable modules and PostgreSQL support, generated OpenAPI/SDK, the `apps/web` application shell, the Living Documentation Portal, and project-derivation commands exist. The README's Current state section says which modules this repository composes. Keycloak login, server-managed human sessions and OTP step-up have local integration qualification; real provider deployment and the remaining identity/access workflows are pending. See [identity and access](docs/project/identity-and-access.md). Use Node.js 24.13.0 and pnpm 11.25.0; run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` to install dependencies and `pnpm validate` before considering substantial work complete. Use [setup](docs/setup.md) for local environment loading and startup. Run individual checks through the scripts in `package.json`. See [validation availability and responsibilities](docs/validation.md) and [CI status](docs/architecture/continuous-integration.md); do not claim a remote check or future capability has run without evidence.

title: API-local Instructions
heading: API-local Instructions
text:
API-local Instructions
Read [the runtime guide](README.md) for source locations, local commands, and the module contract. Read the nested `AGENTS.md` of a module before changing it. Global repository instructions still apply.
Preserve `src/main.ts` ordering: parse configuration, initialize Pino/OpenTelemetry, then dynamically load Fastify and compose `src/app.ts` before listening. Instrumented infrastructure depends on this order.
Keep `src/config.ts` as the runtime environment parser. Change schemas and reference metadata together; client-eligible values must pass explicitly through `clientConfigFrom`.
Shared runtime files never import a module. A module implements the `ApiModule` contract in `src/module.ts` and is composed only in `src/modules.ts`; it owns its contracts, errors, routes, persistence adapter, Prisma model file under `prisma/schema/`, metadata under `prisma/metadata/`, runtime grants under `prisma/runtime-grants/`, migrations, tests, and optional process smoke under `scripts/smoke/`.
Keep TypeBox wire schemas/routes at the Fastify boundary. Domain rules and application operations remain independent of Fastify and Prisma; the adapter owns PostgreSQL and conditional writes.
Keep Prisma schema, reviewed SQL, and semantic metadata coherent under [migration](../../docs/database/migrations.md) and [schema-documentation](../../docs/database/schema-documentation.md) policies. The Prisma CLI alone receives `ORION_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`; runtime uses `ORION_DATABASE_URL`.
Generate the ignored Prisma client with root `pnpm db:generate`. For tracked references, follow the [artifact workflow](../../docs/architecture/backend-execution-and-generated-artifacts.md); root `pnpm references:check` includes fresh migrated PostgreSQL and SDK drift checks.
Use allowlisted diagnostics under [redaction policy](../../docs/security/telemetry-redaction.md). Do not attach request bodies, raw URLs, headers, configuration objects, or arbitrary exception messages to logs/spans. Expected failures are explicit; unexpected failures have one authoritative diagnostic event.
Run focused API `test`, `typecheck`, and `build` scripts as applicable, then root `pnpm validate` before substantial-work handoff. Report unavailable checks honestly.

title: API Runtime

text:
API Runtime
[Setup](../../docs/setup.md) · [API principles](../../docs/api/principles.md) · [OpenAPI](../../docs/generated/api/openapi.json) · [Validation](../../docs/validation.md)
The Fastify API runtime provides configuration, structured logging and tracing, health/lifecycle behavior, the public error envelope, optional PostgreSQL access through Prisma, and optional bearer access-token verification. Product capabilities are [modules](#modules) composed in [`src/modules.ts`](src/modules.ts). The [web application](../web/README.md) consumes the generated API contract through the workspace SDK package (`packages/sdk`). The composed `identity` module implements Keycloak login and server-managed human sessions without handling passwords; see [identity and sessions](#identity-and-sessions).

title: API Runtime
heading: Modules
text:
Modules
A module is one cohesive API capability. It implements the `ApiModule` contract in [`src/module.ts`](src/module.ts): a name, an OpenAPI tag, its requirements (`database`, `authentication`), its executable operations, its public error codes, and an `activate` function that mounts routes once its requirements are configured. Shared runtime files never import a module; [`src/modules.ts`](src/modules.ts) is the only composition point, and dependency rules enforce that boundary.
Keep a module's files together under its name: `src/features/<module>/` for domain, application, persistence, contracts, routes, and errors; `prisma/schema/<module>.prisma` for its models; `prisma/metadata/<module>.json` for table meaning; `prisma/runtime-grants/<module>.sql` for least-privilege runtime access; a reviewed migration; tests under `test/<module>/`; and an optional emitted-process smoke at `scripts/smoke/<module>.ts`. Follow [application boundaries](../../docs/architecture/application-boundaries.md), [dependency rules](../../docs/architecture/dependency-rules.md), and the [database policies](../../docs/database/principles.md). [Orion's reference implementation](../../docs/project-derivation.md#orions-reference-implementation) is a complete example.
Outside production, a module whose requirements are not configured stays unmounted. In production, startup fails instead, so a composed capability cannot silently disappear. Generated OpenAPI and the public error registry always include every composed module, whether or not it is configured locally.

title: API Runtime
heading: Configuration and database access
text:
Configuration and database access
[`config.ts`](src/config.ts) is the sole runtime environment parser; the [generated configuration reference](../../docs/generated/configuration/api.md) owns the setting catalog. `ORION_ENV` is always required. `ORION_DATABASE_URL` enables the database for modules that require it and adds a bounded database check to readiness. `ORION_TOKEN_ISSUER`, `ORION_TOKEN_AUDIENCE`, and `ORION_TOKEN_JWKS_URL` enable bearer authentication and must be configured together.
`ORION_DATABASE_URL` is the restricted runtime credential. Only the Prisma CLI reads `ORION_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`, supplied separately for migration commands; the CLI does not automatically load the API's root `.env.local`. Keep both out of tracked files and do not leave the migration credential in the runtime environment.
The runtime role needs `USAGE` on the application schema plus only the table and column privileges that each module declares in `prisma/runtime-grants/`. It needs no DDL grant. The [database fixture](scripts/migrated-database.ts) provisions separate migration/runtime roles and applies those grants, so integration tests run with the same least-privilege runtime role.
The [release workflow](../../docs/database/release-evolution.md) owns durable migration recording. An empty registry is not permission to rewrite unverified history.

title: API Runtime
heading: Identity and sessions
text:
Identity and sessions
The [`identity` module](src/features/identity/AGENTS.md) owns application principals and PostgreSQL-backed browser sessions under the [identity and session design](../../docs/project/identity-session-design.md). It requires the database, the token settings and the six `TELUNI_` human identity settings, and stays unmounted outside production until they are configured. Login, callback and back-channel logout are public browser/provider routes under `/auth`; session routes and every product module that needs a human authenticate through its session boundary, exposed to other modules only by `src/features/identity/public.ts`. That boundary passes the stored provider access token through the unchanged verifier below, so the cookie never bypasses it. Bearer-only requests without a session are rejected by session-protected operations.
The realm contract is provisioned by [`scripts/identity-realm.ts`](scripts/identity-realm.ts) and qualified against the pinned Keycloak image in [`scripts/keycloak.ts`](scripts/keycloak.ts). Identity tests start that image and PostgreSQL through Testcontainers.

title: API Runtime
heading: Organizations
text:
Organizations
The [`organizations` module](src/features/organizations/AGENTS.md) depends on the identity session boundary. It owns companies, branches, creator memberships, responsibility, standard-role grants and branch scopes, and append-only organization audit under [D-01](../../docs/project/tenant-data-design.md#implementation-status). Every request resolves current tenant access; administrator and manager grants require strong authentication. Company creation is idempotent per principal/key and atomically creates the creator relationships and audit event. Company and branch changes use expected versions and write audit in the same transaction. Branch and audit pagination reject invalid or incorrectly bound cursors. Runtime grants exclude tenant-column changes, audit edits/deletion and membership/grant administration that has no implemented operation.
The [`mail` module](src/features/mail/AGENTS.md) owns the transactional outbound-email outbox under [ADR-0026](../../docs/adr/0026-propose-a-postgresql-outbox-and-smtp-relay-for-transactional-email.md). It requires the database and the `TELUNI_MAIL_` settings (which also need `TELUNI_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`) and stays unmounted outside production until they are configured. Producers enqueue messages inside their own transactions through `src/features/mail/public.ts`; the dispatcher starts when the server is ready, claims due messages with expiring leases, submits them through SMTP at least once with bounded retries, and stops during shutdown drain.
The `invitations` module, composed from the organizations feature, requires organizations and mail and owns company invitations under [D-13](../../docs/project/invitation-delivery-design.md#implementation-status): administrators and branch managers invite by email, and the person signed in with the invited verified address accepts with the credential from the email link in a request body. Organizations keeps working without it when mail is not configured.
The [two-company suite](test/organizations/integration.test.ts) runs against migrated PostgreSQL as the restricted runtime role; its synthetic session port is confined to the test. The [organizations browser journeys](../web/test/e2e/organizations/companies.spec.ts) use the real identity stack. Platform/support access and bulk operations remain pending in PJ-03/PJ-24.

title: API Runtime
heading: Devices
text:
Devices
The [`devices` module](src/features/devices/AGENTS.md) requires identity, organizations, the database and `TELUNI_DEVICE_CODE_KEYS`, and owns screen enrollment, pairing and lifecycle under [ADR-0027](../../docs/adr/0027-propose-device-generated-credentials-and-code-based-enrollment.md) and the [device enrollment design](../../docs/project/device-enrollment-design.md#implementation-status). A player starts an anonymous enrollment with the hash of a credential it generated, shows the returned code, and polls until a person with `devices.manage` on the target branch claims the code in the panel. Device routes authenticate that credential as a bearer token; check-in renews offline authorization for seven days. Unlinking is irreversible and leaves erasure pending until the device confirms it or a person records a controlled reset. Archiving a branch with active screens is refused with `BRANCH_IN_USE`. The [two-company suite](test/devices/integration.test.ts) covers claims, limits, concurrency, scope, rotation and erasure against migrated PostgreSQL.

title: API Runtime
heading: Media
text:
Media
The [`media` module](src/features/media/AGENTS.md) requires identity, organizations, the database and `TELUNI_MEDIA_STORAGE_PATH`, and owns the company media library under [ADR-0028](../../docs/adr/0028-propose-local-content-addressed-media-storage-and-isolated-ffmpeg-processing.md) and the [media library design](../../docs/project/media-library-design.md#implementation-status). A person with `media.upload` creates an item for the company or one branch, then streams its bytes with `PUT .../content` (`application/octet-stream`, exact declared length); uploads alone may run longer than the standard 30-second request limit. An in-process processor inspects and converts each upload with FFmpeg into a display rendition and a thumbnail, and the item becomes `READY` or `REJECTED` with a reason. Content is served with range support, `nosniff` and a sandboxing CSP. Archive, delete (to a 30-day trash), restore and discard use expected versions; registered reference guards block deleting media in use. FFmpeg/ffprobe 6.1 or later are required; production refuses to start without them. The [two-company suite](test/media/integration.test.ts) processes synthetic media with real FFmpeg against migrated PostgreSQL.

title: API Runtime
heading: Identity and contract
text:
Identity and contract
The shared [token verifier](src/authentication.ts) accepts verified `at+jwt` tokens signed with RS256 or ES256 by the configured issuer for the configured audience. It validates expiration and requires nonempty `sub`, valid issuance/expiry timing, a stable `orion_principal_id` UUID, `orion_actor_type=human`, and a string `scope`. It yields the principal ID and the issuer-granted scopes; product modules also enforce current session and application-owned memberships. Stored ownership must survive provider changes; request bodies cannot grant identity or capability. The [authentication policy](../../docs/security/authentication.md) and [ADR-0012](../../docs/adr/0012-verify-jwt-access-tokens-at-the-first-api-boundary.md) govern this boundary. Keycloak is selected and locally qualified; no real environment is provisioned.
Executable module contracts own operations, stable operation IDs, typed inputs/outputs, and expected failures. The [OpenAPI reference](../../docs/generated/api/openapi.json) includes health and every composed module's operations; the [error reference](../../docs/generated/api/errors.md) derives from the shared and module registries.

title: API Runtime
heading: Request protection
text:
Request protection
A module that exposes authenticated routes should apply request limiting before token verification and database access, as the reference module does with a process-local source-IP limit; health probes stay outside it. Exhaustion returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` in the public envelope with a bounded `Retry-After`. This is resource protection, not a product quota.
Process-local limiting uses the direct peer address; trusted proxies are not configured. A multi-replica or reverse-proxy deployment must define shared/edge limiting and trusted client-IP handling before promising fleet-wide or per-user limits.

title: API Runtime
heading: Lifecycle and diagnostics
text:
Lifecycle and diagnostics
`main.ts` validates configuration, initializes Pino/OpenTelemetry, then dynamically imports Fastify, Prisma, and composed modules before listening. Preserve that order for instrumented infrastructure. Incoming W3C trace context propagates; each request receives a fresh server-generated `x-request-id`. Errors follow the [public envelope](../../docs/api/error-contract.md). Logs and traces identify the service by the API package name.
Startup reports initialization, liveness reports process-local health, and readiness becomes unavailable while draining or when a configured database is unavailable. A configured database is probed before readiness and through a bounded readiness check. SIGINT/SIGTERM trigger bounded HTTP, database, and telemetry shutdown.
Logs and exported spans/metric dimensions use allowlisted operational fields. The runtime does not log payloads, raw URLs, headers, configuration objects, or arbitrary exception messages. Unexpected failures produce one sanitized diagnostic occurrence. A readiness failure or a lost response cannot prove that a prior write failed; see [delivery and side effects](../../docs/architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md).

title: Devices Module
heading: Devices Module
text:
Devices Module
This module owns screen (player) enrollment, pairing and lifecycle under [ADR-0027](../../../../../docs/adr/0027-propose-device-generated-credentials-and-code-based-enrollment.md) and the [device enrollment design](../../../../../docs/project/device-enrollment-design.md). Read both before changing behavior.
The device credential is generated on the device and never reaches the server; only its SHA-256 is accepted, stored and compared. Pairing codes are stored only as HMACs under `TELUNI_DEVICE_CODE_KEYS`. Codes, credentials, hashes and client addresses never reach logs, audit details or error bodies.
Every failed claim, whatever the reason (unknown, expired, already claimed, malformed), answers the same `PAIRING_CODE_INVALID` and counts toward the per-principal and per-company limits.
Human operations resolve access through the organizations `CompanyAccessPort` and take its `lockForWrite` (company, membership and branches `FOR SHARE`) before locking enrollment or device rows; do not add another lock order. A device outside the caller's branches answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
Device rows keep the composite `(company_id, id)` key and never change company; moving changes `branch_id` only. Unlinking is irreversible: the device becomes `REVOKED` with erasure `PENDING`, and only the device's confirmation or a person's reset record ends it.
Each human change and erasure confirmation writes its `device_audit_events` row in the same transaction; details hold IDs and settings only. Other modules import only `public.ts` of identity and organizations.

title: Identity Module
heading: Identity Module
text:
Identity Module
This module owns application principals, server-managed human sessions and the session boundary other modules use. Read the [identity and session design](../../../../../docs/project/identity-session-design.md) and the [identity policies](../../../../../docs/project/identity-and-access.md) before changing behavior.
Other modules import only `public.ts`; dependency rules reject imports of this module's internals. Compose dependents after this module in `src/modules.ts` with `requiresModules: ["identity"]`.
Never weaken the ADR-0012 verifier, the CSRF/Origin check, the 30-second provider revalidation or the single-use login attempt to make a flow pass. A Keycloak behavior that does not meet the design is a recorded gap, not a reason to relax a check.
Keep provider calls outside database transactions, credentials out of logs and errors, and the recoverable cookie credential out of storage (only its SHA-256 digest is persisted; provider tokens are sealed).
The realm contract lives in `apps/api/scripts/identity-realm.ts` and is qualified by `test/identity/keycloak-contract.test.ts` against the pinned image in `scripts/keycloak.ts`; change them together.

title: Mail Module
heading: Mail Module
text:
Mail Module
This module owns the transactional outbound-email outbox, its dispatcher and the SMTP adapter (ADR-0026). Read the [delivery section of the invitation and email delivery design](../../../../../docs/project/invitation-delivery-design.md#durable-email-delivery) and the [delivery policy](../../../../../docs/architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md) before changing behavior.
Producers own what a message means: they register its template and enqueue it through `public.ts` inside their own transaction. Do not add producer-specific wording, rules or tables here.
Delivery is at least once. Never claim exactly once, and keep every outcome write guarded by the claim's lease and the pending state so a stale dispatcher or a cancellation is never overwritten.
Secret parameters stay sealed under the mail key ring and are erased at the final state. Recipient addresses, secrets and message bodies never reach logs, spans, metrics or errors; diagnostics carry message IDs and failure classes only.
Retry timing, attempt limits, lease length and retention live in `domain.ts`; change them with the design, its tests and the schema metadata together.

title: Media Module
heading: Media Module
text:
Media Module
This module owns the company media library: images and videos, their processing into playback renditions, storage and lifecycle under [ADR-0028](../../../../../docs/adr/0028-propose-local-content-addressed-media-storage-and-isolated-ffmpeg-processing.md) and the [media library design](../../../../../docs/project/media-library-design.md). Read both before changing behavior.
Uploaded bytes are untrusted. Admission checks the declared type and size; the processor checks the file signature, forces the matching demuxer and reads files only through FFmpeg/ffprobe child processes started by `ffmpeg.ts` (no shell, PATH-only environment, `-protocol_whitelist file`, timeouts, process-group kill, `prlimit` where present). Never pass user text (names, tags) to a tool, and never log tool output, paths, hashes or file names.
Objects are content-addressed per company under `<root>/objects/<companyId>/` and only `storage.ts` builds paths. Publish an object (insert its row and rename the work file) and release one (check references, delete the row, unlink the file) only inside a transaction holding `lockObject` for that hash, so a purge and an upload of the same bytes never lose a file. A row never exists without its file; an orphan file is swept.
Human operations resolve access through the organizations `CompanyAccessPort` and take its `lockForWrite` before locking asset rows; then the asset row, then object locks. A hidden item answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. `PURGED` rows stay for audit and are never visible.
Processing claims rows with a lease and an attempt fencing token; every finishing write checks both, so a superseded attempt changes nothing. Rejections are permanent and release the original; failures retry with backoff up to `mediaPolicy.maxAttempts`.
Modules that reference media register a guard through `public.ts` (`registerReferenceGuard`) and select media only through `requireSelectable`. Deletion and purge refuse while any guard reports a reference. Each human change writes its `media_audit_events` row in the same transaction; details hold IDs, sizes and settings only.

title: Organizations Module
heading: Organizations Module
text:
Organizations Module
This module owns companies (tenants), branches, memberships, standard role and access profile grants, the responsible administrator and organization audit. Read the [tenant data design](../../../../../docs/project/tenant-data-design.md) and the [permission matrix](../../../../../docs/project/identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix) before changing behavior.
Every tenant-owned table with its own `id` keeps `(company_id, id)` unique and every tenant reference composite; the structural suite in `test/organizations/integration.test.ts` enforces it on the migrated schema. Join tables and one-to-one extensions without an `id` follow D-01's key exception. Never grant runtime `UPDATE` on `company_id` or `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on audit events.
Resolve access on every request through `OrganizationService.access`; never cache it beyond the 30-second revocation bound, and never take company, branch or role from a request body as authority. Hidden resources answer `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
Role capabilities live in `domain.ts`; administrator and branch-manager grants count only in strongly authenticated sessions (P12). Add a capability with the module that needs it, not speculatively.
Authority-changing writers lock the company row first, then the involved memberships in ID order, and recheck the actor's current membership and grants inside that transaction (tenant data design rule 5). Reuse `lockAuthority` in `prisma-repository.ts` for grant, status and responsibility writes; invitation writes lock the company, then the invitation, then memberships, and rebuild the actor's access inside the transaction. Do not add another lock sequence. Modules writing tenant data under the company's authority (such as devices) take `lockForWrite` through `CompanyAccessPort`, which holds the company, the actor's membership and the named branches `FOR SHARE`; branch archive runs registered guards so such modules can refuse it with `BRANCH_IN_USE`.
Access profiles (`profile-repository.ts`) combine only `delegableCapabilities` from `domain.ts`; never make administration, settings, branch or member management delegable. A profile's assurance is per capability (`strongCapabilities`), never per label. Resolve a profile's current capabilities on every request; profile writes follow the same lock order, and each edit audits its added and removed capabilities and affected grants.
Grants are added and revoked, never edited in place. Granting company administration and proposing or accepting a responsibility transfer require the responsible administrator (or, for acceptance, the proposed successor) with strong authentication no older than five minutes, checked against the database clock inside the transaction.
Each change writes its audit event in the same transaction, passing to `writeAudit` the branches the event concerns (none for company-level events); branch managers read only events confined to their branches. Member presentation data comes only from identity's `HumanProfilePort` for principals on an authorized page. Other modules import only `public.ts`.
Invitations (`invitation-*.ts`, composed as the separate `invitations` module) follow the [D-13 design](../../../../../docs/project/invitation-delivery-design.md). Never look up principals by email; only the accepting session's verified email binds an invitation. Credentials are stored only as hashes, travel only in request bodies and never reach logs. Each invitation and its email commit in one transaction through the mail outbox, and acceptance revalidates the inviter's current authority without narrowing the grant.

title: Web Application Instructions
heading: Web Application Instructions
text:
Web Application Instructions
Use [the web guide](README.md) for source locations, startup, and browser checks. Global repository instructions still apply.
Product workflows use the generated workspace SDK (`packages/sdk`) as the API boundary. The generic documentation explorer follows its [bounded OpenAPI execution contract](../../docs/architecture/living-documentation.md#safe-local-reading-and-api-exploration). Change API TypeBox contracts and regenerate OpenAPI/SDK through the [artifact workflow](../../docs/architecture/backend-execution-and-generated-artifacts.md); never import API implementation or hand-edit generated types.
Keep URL-owned list scope/cursor and detail IDs in TanStack Router, API-owned state in TanStack Query, and temporary form state in React. Clear cached query data when the in-memory bearer token changes and on sign-out. Never store the session cookie, CSRF token or provider tokens in URLs, storage or logs.
Browser input and UI visibility do not grant permission. Preserve visible authorization denials, stale-version conflicts, idempotency, and unknown-outcome recovery that a module's API defines, without reimplementing business rules in React. Compose module routes and navigation only in `src/modules.tsx`.
`VITE_ORION_API_BASE_URL` is the only public API setting and must be a same-origin path. Keep credentials in memory, never URLs, storage, logs, or generated artifacts; server/development proxy targets remain outside browser configuration.
Maintain exported component examples/metadata beside source under [living documentation ownership](../../docs/architecture/living-documentation.md); regenerate portal data and component Markdown rather than editing generated files.
Run focused `typecheck`, `build`, `bundle:check`, unit/browser/end-to-end checks as applicable, then root `pnpm validate` before substantial-work handoff. See [validation](../../docs/validation.md) for prerequisites and limits.

title: Web Application
heading: Web Application
text:
Web Application
[Setup](../../docs/setup.md) · [Generated API](../../docs/generated/api/openapi.json) · [Living documentation](../../docs/architecture/living-documentation.md) · [Validation](../../docs/validation.md)

The API remains the authority for authorization and business rules.

title: Web Application
heading: Modules
text:
Modules
A web module is the browser side of a product capability. It defines its routes as children of the shared root route, keeps its pages, client calls, styles, and wording in its own `src/<module>/` folder, and exports a navigation link component. [`src/modules.tsx`](src/modules.tsx) is the only composition point: it adds the module's routes to the route tree and its link to the header and home page. Shared shell and portal code never import a module. Module browser journeys belong in `test/e2e/<module>/` and may start their own disposable stack with the shared [end-to-end stack helpers](test/e2e/stack.ts). [Orion's reference implementation](../../docs/project-derivation.md#orions-reference-implementation) is a complete example.
Use the shared [`ErrorNotice`](src/components.tsx) and [`api-client.ts`](src/api-client.ts) for public API failures: pass a module's own stable codes when unwrapping responses and its own wording for them. A failed or lost write is an unknown outcome, never proof that nothing changed.

title: Web Application
heading: Entry and home page
text:
Entry and home page
Teluni composes its own `/` route from the [`workspace` web module](src/workspace/routes.tsx) instead of the shell's generic home page. A visitor without a session (or when the session service is unavailable) goes to `/sign-in`; a signed-in person sees the home page with their first companies, a path to create the first company, and the session's two-step verification state. `/sign-in` sends a signed-in person on to `returnTo` or the home page, and presents the product beside the sign-in action. The header shows Home, Companies, the session entry and, in development only, Documentation.
The Living Documentation Portal is a development aid, not part of the product (owner direction, 2026-10-19). [`src/modules.tsx`](src/modules.tsx) mounts its routes and header link only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true, so the Vite development server serves `/docs` while production builds drop the portal's code and generated pages; [`scripts/check-public-bundle.mjs`](scripts/check-public-bundle.mjs), part of `bundle:check`, fails when portal content reaches `dist/`.

title: Web Application
heading: Identity
text:
Identity
The display name comes from `.orion/project.json` at build time: page titles, the shell brand, and the portal show the repository's own name. The [brand mark](src/assets/brand-mark.svg) and its derived [touch icon](src/assets/brand-touch-icon.png) belong to the repository. The Orion foundation uses the Orion mark; project initialization replaces both files with a neutral placeholder for the project to redesign.
The shell, documentation navigation, and browser favicon consume the SVG directly. Only the Apple touch icon uses a derived 180×180 PNG on the approved `#F8FAFC` light background. After editing the SVG, run `pnpm -C apps/web identity:write` to regenerate that raster through the [export script](scripts/generate-touch-icon.mjs), using the Playwright Chromium installation described in [setup](../../docs/setup.md#prepare-a-clean-checkout). Commit both files, then rebuild. Do not edit the PNG independently. Adjacent live text names the decorative mark for accessibility.
Teluni uses the owner-approved [Connected Tiles identity](../../docs/project/branding/README.md): the selected symbol, a locally served Plus Jakarta Sans variable font with its OFL notice, titlecase live brand text, and blue/teal/navy palette. The runtime SVG is canonical, and `identity:write` derives its touch PNG. The branding guide owns the single identity kit and remaining domain/trademark evidence.

title: Web Application
heading: Run the application
text:
Run the application
Use the canonical [setup guide](../../docs/setup.md) for installation, environment loading, and prerequisites. For an API at `127.0.0.1:3000`, run `pnpm -C apps/web dev`.
Vite forwards the default `/api` browser path to the local API and removes that prefix. `ORION_WEB_API_TARGET` changes only the development-server target. `VITE_ORION_API_BASE_URL` is the sole browser API setting, defaults to `/api`, and must be a same-origin path. A deployed static build needs an equivalent same-origin route/reverse proxy; this guide does not select deployment infrastructure. Server-only URLs and credentials must not enter browser configuration.
Human sign-in uses the server-managed session of the API's `identity` module. The [`identity` web module](src/identity/routes.tsx) provides `/sign-in`, `/account/sessions` and the header's sign-in/sign-out entry. Login is a full navigation to `/api/auth/login`; the browser then holds only the API's `HttpOnly` session cookie, and the session's CSRF token stays in module memory for unsafe requests through the SDK. Sign-out clears all cached query data. `loginHref(returnTo, "strong" | "recent")` starts two-step verification when an operation answers `STRONG_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` or `RECENT_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`; the sessions page offers it directly. The header entry neither queries nor shows the session on `/docs` pages, so the portal still makes no API calls while browsing. Copy is localized through a typed pt-BR/en-US catalog in `src/identity/messages.ts`; no i18n library is selected yet. The API still verifies every business request, and production credentials must never be used in tests.

title: Web Application
heading: Companies and branches
text:
Companies and branches
The [`organizations` module](src/organizations/routes.tsx) provides `/companies` and `/companies/$companyId`, composed with identity in `src/modules.tsx`. A signed-in person can page through their companies and create a company with its initial responsible-administrator membership. Company administration offers two-step verification when required by the API. Strongly authenticated administrators can create, rename and archive branches, edit the company's name/default language/time zone, and read its change history; other members see only the branches their current grants allow. Company and branch pages, the selected company view (`view=settings` or `view=history`) and history pages live in route search parameters, so reload and browser history preserve them. Changing views clears the previous collection's cursor. API queries remain in TanStack Query and all product calls use the generated SDK with the session cookie and in-memory CSRF token.
Company creation retains its idempotency key across a retry. Branch renames and company-settings drafts retain the version observed when editing started even if their queries refetch; stale-version recovery reloads current data for review. A lost settings response blocks another save until current data is loaded. Successful settings changes invalidate the company detail, company lists and history. Authorization denials stay visible, including direct settings/history URLs without the required capability. Copy is localized through `src/organizations/messages.ts` using the shared browser-locale selection in `src/locale.ts`. Administrators with the `members.manage` capability also get a `view=members` page listing memberships with presentation names/emails from each person's last verified sign-in. Suspending, reactivating or removing a member asks for confirmation that keeps the version observed when the action was requested; a conflict or lost response requires reloading before another change, and restoring an administrator offers recent two-step re-authentication. The responsible administrator shows no lifecycle actions. Each member lists their effective grants with branches and expiry; an administrator can add a grant (role, whole company or selected active branches, optional expiry, with the administration role offered only to the responsible administrator) and revoke one after confirmation. The responsible administrator can propose transferring responsibility from an active administrator's row; the company page shows the pending transfer only to its two parties, with accept or decline for the successor and cancel for the proposer, and offers recent two-step re-authentication when the API requires it. Members with the `invitations.manage` capability get a `view=invitations` page: administrators invite by email with a role, scope, branches and optional expiry (administration only by the responsible administrator), branch managers invite operators to the branches they manage, and the list shows each invitation's state and email delivery with resend and confirmed revoke. The public `/invitations/accept` route moves the credential from the link fragment into the tab's session storage, asks the person to sign in, previews the invitation for the matching verified address and accepts it on explicit confirmation. The [organizations browser journeys](test/e2e/organizations/companies.spec.ts) use the disposable [local identity stack](../../docs/setup.md#try-sign-in-locally), which can also be used manually to open `/companies`.
The [`devices` module](src/devices/routes.tsx) provides `/companies/$companyId/screens` and `/companies/$companyId/screens/$deviceId` ("Telas"), linked from the company page for members with `devices.view`. The list filters by branch and status in route search parameters and shows each screen's branch, state, erasure and last check-in. Members with `devices.manage` pair a screen by entering the code it shows, which travels only in the request body, with a name, branch and rotation. The screen page shows the reported model and resolution as the device's own statement, the latest offline deadline the screen could hold, and lets managers rename it, change rotation among the reported values, move it to another branch and unlink it after explicit confirmation; an unlinked screen with pending erasure offers a reset record. Changes keep the version observed when the page loaded, and conflicts or lost responses require a reload. The [screens journey](test/e2e/devices/screens.spec.ts) simulates the player over HTTP against the local identity stack.
